The proposed improvement introduces coordinate binning into micro-grid regions for both pickup and dropoff locations. By discretizing continuous latitude and longitude values into approximate 2-kilometer spatial cells and encoding them as categorical features, the LightGBM model can learn distinct base fares and route-specific pricing multipliers inherent to taxi services. This atomic change leverages the model's native categorical splitting capability to capture non-linear spatial pricing patterns without increasing computational overhead. Predictions will remain clipped to realistic bounds to maintain stability.
